specification.problem: Order finding for Shor's algorithm with N=15, a=2 (order r=4), with the ideal circuit and three assumed gate-imperfection models (systematic, random, combined) on the QFT phase gates. The aim is to compare the success probability with the ideal value and define an operational error threshold sigma_c.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One tiny instance: t=4 counting qubits, 4 work qubits, N=15, a=2. The built unitary contains H, controlled modular multiplications, and an inverse QFT whose controlled-phase angles are perturbed by explicit numeric error values. Excluded: the paper's analytic threshold formula and precise error definitions, scaling with N beyond a numerical sigma_c, and classical decoding. Decoding is documented but is not part of the unitary.

symbols.meaning: multiplicative order of a mod N
counting register integer, little-endian x=sum_k x_k 2^k
fixed systematic relative and absolute angle errors
random angle offset of phase gate j, zero mean, width sigma
probability mass on counting outcomes x with x/2^t within rounding of s/r
largest sigma with averaged P_succ >= eta times ideal

equations.label: Modular multiplication unitary
equations.description: Controlled modular exponentiation for y in 0..14. Values y>=15 are left fixed so that U is a permutation and hence unitary.
assumptions: Compiled with explicit classical a and N
Work register is 4 qubits, y=1 initially

equations.label: Ideal output distribution
equations.description: Ideal outcome peaks at x/2^t near s/r. For t=4, r=4 the peaks are x=0,4,8,12 with probability 1/4 each.
assumptions: r divides 2^t exactly in this instance

equations.label: Systematic error model
equations.description: The same fixed angle error is applied to every controlled-phase gate.
equations.justification: The abstract names systematic errors without defining them, so this is an assumed definition.

equations.label: Random and combined error models
equations.description: Independent random offsets per gate, or a fixed offset plus random offsets. Several seeds are averaged.
equations.justification: The abstract names the three categories without definitions.
assumptions: The distribution (e.g. Gaussian or uniform) is my choice

equations.label: Success probability and threshold
equations.description: Operational numerical threshold with cutoff fraction eta, e.g. 1/2.
equations.justification: The abstract says an error threshold is given for N but not its form; this is an operational stand-in.
assumptions: This is not the paper's analytic threshold

equations.label: Ideal inverse QFT gate decomposition
equations.latex: \mathrm{QFT}^{-1}:\ \text{H on qubit } k \text{ and CP}(-\pi/2^{m}) \text{ between qubits separated by } m,\ \text{then bit-reversal swaps}
equations.description: The inverse QFT is built from H and controlled-phase gates with ideal angles -theta_m, which the error models perturb.

registers.name: work
registers.role: holds y mod 15, little-endian, initial value 1

steps.description: Apply H to every counting qubit, giving a uniform superposition over x. This is the input preparation for the controlled exponentiation.
Apply controlled U^(2^k) from counting qubit k onto the work register, with U the multiplication by 2 mod 15 (a cyclic bit permutation). Optionally add small Rz rotations after these gates.
Apply the inverse QFT on the counting register with swaps, with the controlled-phase angles perturbed per the chosen error model using explicit numeric values.
Outside the unitary: simulate the output distribution, measure the counting register to get x, and evaluate P_succ against the ideal value and sigma_c, averaging over seeds for the random errors.

specification.measurement: Measure the counting register in the computational basis, outside the built unitary.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Continued fractions of x/2^t give r, then gcd(a^(r/2)±1, N) gives factors. Compute P_succ against the ideal value, and average over seeds for the random errors.
assumptions: The error models are my definitions, since the abstract does not define them
N=15, a=2, t=4 chosen as the smallest instance
The qualitative claim (robust to systematic, vulnerable to random errors) is only tested numerically on this single instance
missing_information: The analytic threshold formula as a function of N
The error distributions and gate set used by the paper
